Senator Ted Cruz (Republican, Texas) on Tuesday defended Trump after the latter claimed that two "big, strong" firefighters had carried him to safety near the World Trade Center site after the September 11 terrorist attacks, fearing buildings could collapse.

Trump had previously spoken without evidence about leading a group of people to the World Trade Center site to help with the aftermath. On Tuesday, at an event commemorating first responders to 9/11, he claimed he had feared a building near the WTC site would collapse on him "personally," after which firefighters arrived and carried him away.

Trump said: "They grabbed me and said, 'We've got to get out of here.' They actually picked me up... and just carried me out like that."

Trump told similar stories in 2016 and 2021, but his remarks immediately drew swift backlash.

The senator said: "9/11 was 25 years ago." He went on to stress that Trump was a New Yorker, and he did not doubt "that he was expressing what he experienced personally at the time."

He added: "It was a traumatic experience for all of us."

Cruz's defence failed to convince critics on social media. A number of X users, including left-wing Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, reminded their followers that the senator had "liked" a pornographic video shared on September 11, 2017.

Piker wrote: "So I'm not surprised he would defend Trump like this."

One user quipped: "Never forget, except for Donald Trump, who can forget." Another mocked that his defence was exactly the sort of thing "a sycophant like Ted Cruz would do... especially since Trump once mocked his wife's appearance."

The White House also defended Trump. Meanwhile, Trump posted a lengthy statement on Truth Social insisting he had been near the WTC site "obviously not on the day the buildings came down, but shortly thereafter."
